item.title: [NEWS] Race Against the Clock or Ticketing Smoke & Mirrors? What’s Actually Disappearing Ahead of TX2’s 2027 Tour
item.dc:creator: Mighn Taghor
item.description:
• Shows really are shrinking, but don’t panic: the TX2 camp is flashing low-ticket warnings, yet a “sold out” tag at one vendor often doesn’t mean the doors are locked at the official box office.
  • Prague plot twists (and across the rest of Europe): Czechia’s Rock Café has already burned through 50% of its tickets without sounding any loud alarms, and the tour map is packed with venue curveballs.
  • EU VIP passes are spin the bottle: Sound Rink is handling the packages, but with zero public counters out there, dragging your feet means risking a total L.

Not All Ticket Vendors Are Built the Same (Where It’s Actually Getting Tight)

The latest low ticket warnings coming out of Evan Thomas’s camp for most of the UK/EU run aren’t just empty TikTok hype - still, it pays to check the actual box offices before throwing extra cash at scalpers.

The UK is feeling the squeeze the hardest. In Nottingham (March 12), the promoter already slapped on a “Last few tickets” badge, Glasgow (March 10) is flashing “Limited Availability” on Ticketmaster, and London (March 4) completely wiped out its wheelchair allocation. Nothing sums up how ticketing works better than Manchester (March 9), though: Gigantic is already down to a waiting list and the venue’s own access area is gone, yet Ticketmaster UK still has tickets sitting there under “Limited Availability”.

Here in Warsaw (Feb 20, Hydrozagadka), it’s the exact same story: Tier 1 and family passes at Knock Out are Sold Out, while Tier 2 is still floating around. The takeaway? When one outlet (or resale sharks like Viagogo/StubHub with their “Almost sold out” scare banners) hits zero, the official promoter often still has regular-priced tickets waiting. (For some US context: January’s ShipRocked 2027 cruise sold out every single cabin, and May’s Welcome To Rockville already burned through its RV camping spots, even though festival passes themselves are still up for grabs.)

Prague Plot Twists and Good Ol’ Tour Map Chaos

Against all that noise, Prague (Feb 21, Rock Café) is worth a closer look. Nobody’s hitting the red panic button yet, but Czech promoter RFP Concerts put an honest counter right on the page: 50% of tickets are already gone. Half the room is spoken for before half the crew even thought about making the cross-border trip.

The rest of the mainland map brings plenty of classic punk-rock disorder too: Tampere’s Olympia shut its doors and left fans hanging on refunds, Milan’s ticketing sites can’t agree on whether it’s Santeria Toscana 31 or Lime Club, and Switzerland’s PETZI has Solothurn marked as postponed - even while local box offices keep spitting out tickets.

EU VIP Passes: Sound Rink and Spin the Bottle With Fate

If you’re aiming for more than just throwing elbows in the pit (like actually meeting the band and handing over that Warsaw pigeon poster), Sound Rink (eu.soundrink.com) is running the EU/UK VIP packages, just like the band confirmed back in June. Bailey Spinn threw her own separate VIP Upgrade into the mix there too.

The catch? TX2’s own VIPs are sitting in a total info black hole - there are zero public counters online showing how many spots are left. With regular tickets, you can still shop around between official box offices, but if you wait around on a VIP pass, you’re playing spin the bottle with fate.

Source: TX2 OFFICIAL / Sound Rink / Promoters

item.title: [SPOTTED] Found Online: Even Montreal Skeptics Couldn’t Look Away (And Yes, Part of the Crowd Bounced Right After TX2)
item.dc:creator: Mighn Taghor
item.description:
Whenever Reddit puts that tired old record back on - claiming TX2 is “just algorithms and empty TikTok hype” - it pays to look at write-ups from actual clubs, especially the ones coming from outside the fan bubble. A killer take just popped up on the Canadian outlet MetalUniverse.net, where Molly Caisse-Vee reviewed the show at Montreal’s Club Soda (Nov 17).

The best part? She admits right out of the gate that TX2’s music isn’t really her cup of tea - which makes what she saw from behind the lens hit even harder. Even though Evan and the crew were “only” opening for Catch Your Breath, something went down on the floor that sums up just how big this whole thing has gotten:

  • A show inside a show: TX2 didn’t have to beg for the headliner’s crowd to pay attention. They brought out their own fiercely loyal crew who screamed back every single lyric on the setlist, caught the band for a quick hangout near the entrance during the intermission, and then… literally headed straight home as soon as TX2’s set wrapped. A pretty loud reality check for anyone who thinks an opener is just there as background noise.
  • A straight time-warp to the VIVA / MTV era: Molly also called out the band’s visual bite - all black and red, rocking that slightly provocative skater-kid vibe straight out of 2000s music videos (she compared it to classics on Canada’s MusiquePlus, which for us back home screams late-night VIVA and old-school MTV).

Our take: Love or hate Evan Thomas’s whole persona, impartial reviews like this expose why the 2027 European tour is chewing through ticket tiers so fast. When a metal-site reviewer walks in thinking “not really my sound,” still gives props for stage presence, and has to note that plenty of fans showed up exclusively for the support act - it means this machine actually delivers live, not just in vertical reels on your phone screen.

Source: Molly Caisse-Vee / MetalUniverse.net

item.title: [NEWS] Bailey Spinn Joins TX2 for Their 2027 European & UK Tour
item.dc:creator: Mighn Taghor
item.description:
We finally know who's warming up the crowd for TX2's upcoming invasion of Europe. Taking the stage right before Evan Thomas and the crew is American singer-songwriter Bailey Spinn. This run will mark her very first time playing live across Europe and the UK.

Who Is Bailey Spinn and Where'd She Come From?

Born in 2002 and hailing from Virginia, Bailey Rose Spinnenweber took the classic modern route: straight from quick internet virals to live stages. Back in 2020, she blew up on TikTok with short POV skits, pulling in millions of followers within a few months before dropping out of her marketing degree to go all-in on social media. Music came later - first she built up momentum with YouTube covers (her take on Olivia Rodrigo's "Traitor" racked up 1.5 million views in a single month), and by 2023 she kicked off her own originals, starting with the single "romance is dead" and the "my worst enemy" EP.

Even though the music press loves slapping pop-punk and alt-rock labels on her - throwing around names like Evanescence, Paramore, and Sleeping With Sirens as influences - her actual tracks feel super polished and pretty one-note. Following her 2025 debut album "loser", she dropped her sophomore record, "death & devotion", on November 13, 2026. Despite some solid guest spots from familiar faces in the scene - including Kellin Quinn (Sleeping With Sirens), Lee Jennings (The Funeral Portrait), Vlado Saric (Melrose Avenue), and TX2 himself on the four-minute track "silent anymore" - the whole thing stays locked in a very safe, soft-radio lane. It's the kind of sound that fits a morning traffic jam in the American suburbs way better than the raw, untamed rebellion Evan brings to the stage night after night.

The Collab and the Warsaw Stop

Their studio fling on "silent anymore" worked out well enough to spark a joint tour. When the mid-November announcements rolled out, Evan Thomas put it bluntly: after years of watching each other come up in the scene, they finally get to take it over together - kicking off with Bailey's first-ever run across Europe and the UK. She's locked in for both the March UK leg and mainland dates, including the sole Polish stop tracked in our upcoming tour dates:

  • When: February 20, 2027 (Saturday)
  • Where: Warsaw, Hydrozagadka Club (11 Listopada 22)
  • Lineup: TX2 (headliner) + Bailey Spinn (support)

For the local crew quietly hoping for a homegrown opener to kick things off at Hydrozagadka, this pick might come as a bit of a curveball. Looking at the pacing of the night, though, the setup is pretty straightforward: the American singer's tidy, predictable set will serve as a sharp contrast to the genre-bending chaos TX2 unleashes live. In practice, we're getting a chill, easygoing appetizer that'll let everyone save their energy for the absolute riot the headliner is guaranteed to bring.

Source: Punkinfocus

item.title: [NEWS] THE ETERNAL STRUGGLE FOR SURVIVAL IN TX2'S NEW VIDEO - 'I AM THE ENEMY' IS A SURPRISINGLY MATURE TREATISE ON OPPRESSION
item.dc:creator: Mighn Taghor
item.description:
At first glance, TX2's new music video for 'I Am The Enemy' seems to play purely with absurdity. Beneath the low-budget costumes, however, lies a poignant allegory colliding the raw naturalism of nature docs - think hatchling sea turtles massacred by seagulls - with the traumatic aesthetic of the Normandy landings. The beach becomes a battleground for the right to exist, forcing a defenseless outcast to abandon the role of the victim just to stay alive.

The video seamlessly weaves a classic 'Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles' trope into this brutal realism. Cornered and hunted, the young creature is forced to master combat to survive. It serves as the ultimate visual counterpart to the track itself, where Evan Thomas dissects the mechanics of alienation: when the world denies you the right to live on your own terms, simply fighting to survive automatically brands you as 'the enemy' in the eyes of society.

This symbolism peaks inside the bunker, where the protagonist comes face-to-face with the ruthless Crab Commander. This grotesque figure is the literal embodiment of a rigid system, representing the song's 'tradition and authority.' Clad in a hard shell of conformity and an officer's cap, the crab never gets his own claws dirty in the sand - he deploys his seagulls to pacify anyone trying to reach the ocean. When he finally removes his cap to reveal a medieval flail hidden underneath, the message hits with crystal clarity: behind the facade of rules and social order, there is always raw violence. Through a deceptively simple, campy lens, TX2 delivers a stark reminder that against a soulless system, refusing to be a victim is the only way out.

Source: YouTube Official Music Video

item.title: [NEWS] TX2 Unleashes New Single 'I AM THE ENEMY' Ahead of Video Premiere
item.dc:creator: Mighn Taghor
item.description:
It is officially out - TX2's new single 'I AM THE ENEMY' has hit streaming platforms (bundled digitally as a two-track drop alongside 'Witch Hunt'). Speaking to the press, Evan Thomas explained the track was written from a place of owning who he is in a world where his identity stays under constant scrutiny, adding that if his refusal to change makes him a villain, he has no issue wearing the crown. That unapologetic punk punch sets a fierce tone ahead of the 2027 European club run and the Warsaw show at Hydrozagadka - browse the full release catalog in our discography.

Source: Kerrang! / Rock 'N' Load

item.title: [NEWS] New Collab Drop: TX2 Guests on Bailey Spinn's 'silent anymore'
item.dc:creator: Mighn Taghor
item.description:
On November 13, rising alt-rock vocalist Bailey Spinn dropped her heaviest sophomore record to date, 'death & devotion' (via AWAL), featuring TX2 on track #8, 'silent anymore'. Sharing guest billing with Kellin Quinn (Sleeping With Sirens), The Funeral Portrait, and Melrose Avenue, Evan Thomas and crew bring gritty crossover weight to the track while already fueling social feeds with unhinged nurse-costume Shorts alongside Bailey on YouTube and X. Marking another sharp link-up with female voices in modern heavy alt-rock following DeathbyRomy on 'Feed', this drop keeps momentum rolling before the upcoming tour dates and joins the catalog tracked in our discography.

Source: Rock 'N' Load / idobi

item.title: [NEWS] Rumor Confirmed: 'Seagulls and Crab Commander' Is the Official 'I AM THE ENEMY' Video Plot
item.dc:creator: Mighn Taghor
item.description:
Remember our recent rumor about seagulls and a Crab Commander from an LA casting sheet? We now have solid confirmation it was no casting troll - it is the actual storyline for the 'I AM THE ENEMY' music video premiering on YouTube on November 17 at 9:00 PM CET. Backstage production listings tie the track title directly to 'Crab Leader' and 'Seagull Soldier' roles in a plot about a turtle seeking revenge for a D-Day-style seagull beach invasion, while the YouTube premiere artwork already shows a soldier in a WWII helmet and a strapped-on turtle shell screaming amid beach explosions. Once again, TX2 blends combat intensity with B-movie camp absurdity - dive into the roots of this aesthetic in our wtf TX2 overview.

Source: YouTube Premiere / Backstage

item.title: [NEWS] Tour Check: Zero Cancellations, Locked Rockville Date, and Milan Venue Mismatch
item.dc:creator: Mighn Taghor
item.description:
We checked TX2's official tour widget alongside the November 13 press routing: zero shows were cancelled, postponed, or newly added over the past week. Both the North American 'Not Broken Enough Tour' with Catch Your Breath (hitting New Haven tonight through December 5 in Oklahoma City) and the February-March 2027 EU/UK headlining leg - including Warsaw's Hydrozagadka stop - remain locked in, with fresh low-ticket warnings flagged across most UK and European dates. Two key details stand out: TX2's Welcome to Rockville 2027 slot is now pinned to Sunday, May 9, while the official Bandsintown widget still lists Milan (Feb 26, 2027) at Santeria Toscana 31 despite local promoter ticketing already pointing to Lime Club Milano - track every confirmed stop in our tour schedule and check the Warsaw fan action on our main page.

Source: TX2 Official Tour / Rock 'N' Load

item.dc:creator: Mighn Taghor

Detractors on alternative boards dismiss the anti-authority hooks as recycled clichés chasing viral clicks, while longtime fans argue Evan Thomas is deliberately leaning into self-aware provocation - baiting the 'poser' comments to hijack platform algorithms ahead of the November 17 video drop and next year's European run. Dig deeper into how this polarization works in our wtf TX2 guide.

Source: YouTube Shorts @TX2OFFICIAL / Reddit

item.dc:creator: Mighn Taghor
item.description:

Packing 11 songs (starting with 'Infamous' and closing on 'I Would Hate Me Too') into an unforgiving 35-minute support window requires brutal discipline: zero dead air between tracks, seamless beat-matched transitions, and trimmed second verses to prioritize massive choruses and crushing breakdowns. If this nonstop adrenaline carries over to the European run, Warsaw is in for absolute mayhem - check out the fan campaign on our main page.

Source: AXS Tabernacle / Setlist.fm
